title: Singleton
desc: Ensures a class has only one instance and provides a global point of access to it.
problem:
• User drives UserService / OrderService / ReportService; each needs Config.
• Call order is not fixed—any service may run first.
• Each service copies if config == null: config = new Config() → multiple instances.
solution:
• User still calls doWork(); services only call Config.getInstance().
• The null-check and construction live once inside Config.
• First caller creates it; every service shares that instance.

title: Factory Method
desc: Provides an interface for creating objects, but lets subclasses decide which class to instantiate.
problem:
• Client code needs to create different types of objects (e.g. Plane, Truck, Ship).
• The client contains conditional logic and knows about all concrete classes.
• Adding a new type requires modifying client code (violates Open/Closed Principle).
• Object creation logic is scattered and duplicated across the application.
• Client is tightly coupled to concrete classes.
solution:
• Define a factory interface/class for creating products (e.g. Transport).
• Concrete factory decides which concrete product to instantiate.
• Client code works with the factory and the product interface, not concrete classes.
• To add a new type, add a new product and update the factory (client code unchanged).
• Centralizes and encapsulates object creation logic.
before:
plane = new Plane(); plane.fly()
truck = new Truck(); truck.drive()
ship = new Ship(); ship.sail()
// three types; three different method names
reuse: Factory Pattern Infographic_ Before and After (1).png

title: Abstract Factory
desc: Create related product families through a factory interface.
problem: Client news every carrier concrete and calls drive / sail / fly separately.
solution: Pick a family factory; create as Transport; one transport() loop.
before:
dt = new DHLTruck(); dt.drive()
ds = new DHLShip();  ds.sail()
dp = new DHLPlane(); dp.fly()
ut = new UPSTruck(); ut.drive()
us = new UPSShip();  us.sail()
up = new UPSPlane(); up.fly()
after:
dhl = new DHLFactory()
dp = dhl.createPlane(); ds = dhl.createShip(); dt = dhl.createTruck()
ups = new UPSFactory()
up = ups.createPlane(); us = ups.createShip(); ut = ups.createTruck()
fleet = [dp, ds, dt, up, us, ut]
for t in fleet: t.transport()

title: Builder
desc: Separate construction steps from the representation being assembled.
problem:
• House grows telescoping constructors (rooms/doors/windows + pool/trees/…).
• Client passes long positional bool lists—unclear which flag is which.
• Adding a feature forces new overloads and updates every call site.
solution:
• HouseBuilder names each step; ConcreteHouseBuilder adds extras.
• HouseDirector encodes recipes (simple / family); Client can also chain steps.
• Same houses; readable construction; product is House.
before:
houseA = new House(1, 1, 1)
houseB = new House(2, 2, 1, false, false, true, true)
houseC = new House(4, 3, 3, true, false, false, true)
houseD = new House(2, 1, 2, false, true, false, false)
houseE = new House(6, 4, 5, true, true, true, true)
// five houses; magic bool positions
after:
director = new HouseDirector()
houseA = director.buildSimpleHouse(new ConcreteHouseBuilder())
houseB = new ConcreteHouseBuilder().addWindow().addWindow()
    .addDoor().addDoor().addRoom().addStatues().addGarden().getResult()
houseC = director.buildFamilyHouse(new ConcreteHouseBuilder())
houseD = new ConcreteHouseBuilder().addWindow().addWindow()
    .addDoor().addRoom().addRoom().addTrees().getResult()
houseE = new ConcreteHouseBuilder()
    .addWindow().addWindow().addWindow().addWindow().addWindow().addWindow()
    .addDoor().addDoor().addDoor().addDoor()
    .addRoom().addRoom().addRoom().addRoom().addRoom()
    .addPool().addTrees().addStatues().addGarden().getResult()
// same five houses; named steps / director recipes
pnodes:
+ House(windows, doors, rooms)
+ House(windows, doors, rooms, pool)
+ House(windows, doors, rooms, pool, tree)
+ House(windows, doors, rooms, pool, tree, statues)
+ House(windows, doors, rooms, pool, tree, statues, garden)
snodes:
+ rooms: int
+ doors: int
+ windows: int

title: Adapter
case: XML stock data and JSON analytics
desc: Translate an existing interface into the interface a client expects.
problem: The stock app supplies XML; the analytics library requires JSON.
solution: Adapter inherits AnalyticsService and composes JsonAnalyticsLibrary; converts then delegates.
before:
xml = provider.getStockData()
json = convertXmlToJson(xml)
report = library.analyze(json)
// same stock report; client does the conversion
snodes:
- library: JsonAnalyticsLibrary
+ analyze(xml): Report
- convert(xml): JSON

title: Bridge
desc: Separate two independent dimensions so both can evolve independently.
problem: Each shape/color combination requires another subclass.
solution: Shapes hold a Color reference instead of encoding color in inheritance.

title: Facade
desc: Expose a simple entry point to a complex subsystem.
problem: Every client coordinates codecs, bitrate conversion, and audio repair.
solution: A facade orchestrates the subsystem behind one conversion call.
before:
codec = CodecFactory.extract(file)
raw = BitrateReader.read(file, codec)
video = BitrateReader.convert(raw, mp4)
result = AudioMixer.fix(video)
// export file as mp4 via subsystem steps
after:
result = new VideoConverter().convert(file, "mp4")
// same mp4 export; one facade call

title: Proxy
desc: A stand-in object that controls access to a real service without changing its interface.
problem:
• The real service is expensive to create or use (e.g. database, remote API, large object).
• Repeated queries can be slow and waste resources.
• The client may need to handle initialization or access control logic.
• We want extra behavior (caching, logging, access control) without changing client code.
solution:
• Introduce a proxy that implements the same interface as the real service.
• The proxy controls access, adding lazy init, caching, logging, or access control.
• Client uses the same interface—only the class it instantiates changes.
• Adds: caching, lazy initialization, optional access control and logging.
before:
db = new ExpensiveDatabaseService()
r1 = db.query("users")
r2 = db.query("users")
// two "users" results; two expensive hits
after:
db = new DatabaseProxy()
r1 = db.query("users")
r2 = db.query("users")
// same two "users" results; second from cache
snodes:
- realService: DatabaseService
- cache: Map
+ query(key): Result
- getRealService()

title: Composite
desc: Treat individual objects and recursive groups through one interface.
problem: Pricing code distinguishes products from nested boxes repeatedly.
solution: A box sums child prices; each child follows the same contract.
after:
total = order.getPrice()
// same total; one getPrice() on OrderItem

title: Template Method
desc: Fix an algorithm’s order while subclasses implement selected steps.
problem: Format-specific miners duplicate the processing and reporting pipeline.
solution: Move the sequence into a base method; override extraction only.

title: Strategy
desc: Make alternative algorithms interchangeable through a shared contract.
problem: A navigator grows conditionals for road, walking, and transit routes.
solution: Delegate routing to a strategy selected by the client.
before:
road = roadRoute(a, b)
walk = walkRoute(a, b)
transit = transitRoute(a, b)
// three routes; client branches per mode
snodes:
- strategy: RouteStrategy
+ setStrategy(s)
+ buildRoute(a, b): Route

title: State
desc: Delegate behavior to an object representing the current state.
problem: Publication rules accumulate in a switch over document status.
solution: Each state handles publish and can transition the document.
before:
doc.status = "draft"
doc.status = "moderation"   // submit
doc.status = "published"    // admin approve
// draft → moderation → published via status ifs
after:
doc = new Document(new Draft())
doc.publish(user)   // enters moderation
doc.publish(admin)  // becomes published
// same draft → moderation → published path

title: Observer
case: Editor events notify logging and email
desc: Notify registered subscribers when a publisher emits an event.
problem: Editor logic directly invokes concrete logging and email services.
solution: Publish an event; subscribers handle their own reactions.
before:
editor.saveFile()
logger.write(file.name)
mailer.send(file.name)
// save + log + email; client wires reactions
after:
events.subscribe("save", new LogListener())
events.subscribe("save", new EmailListener())
editor.saveFile()
// same save + log + email; listeners react
snodes:
- listeners: EventListener[0..*]
+ subscribe(type, listener)
+ notify(type, data)

title: Command
desc: Represent a request as an object that can be invoked and undone.
problem: Buttons and shortcuts duplicate editing actions without shared undo.
solution: Bind both triggers to a command; store successful edits in history.
after:
paste = new PasteCommand(editor, text)
pasteButton.bind(() => app.execute(paste))
shortcut.bind(() => app.execute(paste))
pasteButton.click(); shortcut.press()
// same two pastes via shared command
snodes:
- editor: Editor
- backup: String
+ execute(): Boolean
+ undo()
